data: India's heavy-lift pad — GSLV Mk III / LVM3 to Chandrayaan-3 and the upcoming Gaganyaan crew programme

Second Launch Pad at Satish Dhawan Space Centre on Sriharikota Island, 13.7°N on India's east coast. First flight PSLV-C6 in May 2005; supports both the PSLV and the heavier LVM3 (formerly GSLV Mk III). Lifted Chandrayaan-2 (July 2019), Chandrayaan-3 (July 2023, the successful lunar lander), and is the planned Gaganyaan crew pad for India's first indigenous human spaceflight. First Launch Pad (FLP, ~1990s) sits next door for smaller manifests. Coordinates from ISRO + DGCA records.

Sriharikota Island on India's east coast, 13.7°N — closer to the equator than Cape Canaveral, with the Bay of Bengal corridor empty downrange. The Second Launch Pad (SLP) handles ISRO's heavy-lift programme: PSLV manifests, LVM3 (formerly GSLV Mk III), Chandrayaan-1 (October 2008, lunar orbiter/impactor), Chandrayaan-2 (July 2019, lost on landing), Chandrayaan-3 (July 2023, successful soft landing near the south pole), and the planned Gaganyaan crewed missions. The First Launch Pad next door handles smaller PSLV / SSLV manifests and hosted the Mangalyaan Mars launch (November 2013).
India's first lunar mission; confirmed widespread water on the Moon
First soft-landing near the lunar south pole
ISRO's heavy strap-on PSLV variant — Chandrayaan-1 + Mars Orbiter
First landing near the lunar south pole
Long March 2D / 4B / 4C polar-orbit workhorse — Yaogan, Gaofen, weather sats
Iran's orbital launch site: Safir put Omid, Iran's first home-built satellite, in orbit in 2009
South Korea's spaceport: Naro-1 (2009-13) and the home-built Nuri rocket since 2021
China's crewed-spaceflight pad — every Shenzhou crew
Europe's Soyuz pad: first Soyuz outside Baikonur or Plesetsk (2011), 27 launches, eight for Galileo
North Korea's satellite launch site: Unha rockets (2012, 2016) and Chollima-1 (2023)
